terms.meaning: The social science that studies the state, government and people's political activity.
The Greek word for city-state. "Politics" comes from it.
The practical side of the problems of state and government.
The Legislature, the Executive and the Judiciary.

items.name: Who started systematic study of politics
items.formula: The Greeks. Egyptians, Persians, Indians and others had ideas, but not a system.
items.example: Socrates and his disciple Plato were great political thinkers.

items.name: Plato's famous book
items.formula: "Republic". It was the first to discuss the nature and work of state and government.
items.example: Plato was a disciple of Socrates.

items.name: Father of Political Science
items.example: His book "The Politics" was the first book on the subject.

items.name: India's work on political principles
items.example: It holds much on how a state is run.

items.name: Garner's definition
items.formula: Political Science starts and ends with the state.
items.example: So the state is the central subject.

items.name: Paul Janet's definition
items.formula: The science of the origin and principles of the state.
items.example: It stresses where the state came from.

items.name: Ideas it explains
items.formula: Monarchy, freedom, justice, laws, equality, good government, war and peace.
items.example: It explains how these ideas began and grew.

items.name: How it helps a state's future
items.formula: The past and present help in planning ahead.
items.example: It helps build a modern welfare state.

items.name: Institutions it explains
items.formula: Political parties, the federal system, local bodies, and the Constitution and laws.
items.example: It also covers the Legislature, Executive and Judiciary.

items.name: What it does for people
items.formula: It builds political awareness, good leaders and good citizens.
items.example: It helps officials find solutions to people's problems.

items.name: Beyond one country
items.example: It shows the value of peace and co-operation among nations.

mistakes.text: "Republic" is by Plato and "The Politics" is by Aristotle. Don't swap them.
Aristotle is the Father of Political Science, though Plato wrote about the state first.
Politics and Political Science are not the same: politics is the practical side, political science the whole study.
